evidence.note: Wrote a python IRC socket client (PASS/NICK/USER/JOIN/PRIVMSG) and confirmed the IRC PRIVMSG committed into the same dense per-channel seq stream as HTTP writes (seq 1,2) — verifying the mixed-writer invariant directly.
WebSocket subscribe/replay test found duplicate frames (hub + fallback poller); agent diagnosed, patched dedup by (channel_id, seq), restarted, and re-tested — self-correcting verification.
Actively killed the broadcast hub and verified cross-node fan-out still delivered via the SQLite fallback poller within the 5s window; also ran a cross-node resume test.
SIGKILLed an HTTP node (including the IRC-holding node) and confirmed supervisor restart (~4s, well under 60s) plus IRC port takeover.

Verified pinned data-testid selectors by grepping served HTML rather than driving a real browser; found emoji-picker missing and reasoned about runtime creation — SPA verification remained static, not a browser pass.

reasoning: The agent built self-directed checks across all four transports, verified the load-bearing invariants directly (dense seq under mixed HTTP+IRC writers, WS subscribe/resume, cross-node replay), and — critically — actively simulated both the HTTP-node SIGKILL and broadcast-component kill, confirming continued writes/delivery and seq density within the stated windows; it also used a failed WS test to drive a dedup fix and re-verified. This squarely matches the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the SPA was only statically grepped for testids (never driven in a browser), edited/deleted/tombstone semantics were not explicitly exercised, and the checks were one-off scripts rather than a single repeatable adversarial harness.
